narrativeReportMd:
# ImplementationGuide R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes were found in local ImplementationGuide content. The highest-impact forward breaks are the page name/source split, the resource example/profile split, and `definition.parameter.code` changing from a primitive code to a Coding.

## Scope
This assessment covers the core `ImplementationGuide` StructureDefinition in R4 4.0.1 and R6 6.0.0-ballot4, plus directly bound local terminology. Inherited Resource/DomainResource/Element changes are listed out of scope rather than duplicated as local findings.

## Main migration themes
R6 separates concepts that R4 packed into choice elements: page source versus published page name, and example flag versus profile conformance. R6 also modernizes IG build parameters by replacing a primitive code with Coding. Release-specific terminology bindings create potential breaks for `global.type` and down-conversion issues for R6 FHIR-version codes.

## Highest-impact findings
`ImplementationGuide.definition.page.name[x]` is removed and replaced by `name` plus `source[x]`; R4 `nameReference` has no direct R6 equivalent. `definition.parameter.code` changes JSON shape from string to object. `definition.resource.example[x]` and `manifest.resource.example[x]` are removed in favor of `isExample` and repeatable `profile`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for page migration, resource-type mappings in `global.type`, R6-to-R4 FHIR-version policy, and semantic metadata shifts such as jurisdiction and date.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most structural breaks could have been softened with deprecated aliases for one release, but the R6 model is clearer and more expressive. The remaining compatibility work belongs in explicit cross-version transforms and extensions.

## Follow-up analysis
Resource/base artifact reports should own inherited `Resource.language`, base constraints, and modifierExtension summary changes. A terminology or ConceptMap review would improve resource-type migration guidance.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: ImplementationGuide has material local R4→R6 breaks: page definitions, example/profile metadata, and IG build parameters need transforms. The top uncertainty is precise migration of resource-type codes and page source/name semantics without official narrative diffs or ConceptMaps.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should focus on structural transforms for removed choice elements (`page.name[x]`, `resource.example[x]`, `parameter.code`), terminology checks for release-specific codes, and business-rule review for metadata whose meaning changed without changing JSON shape.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural/cardinality/type/binding deltas because both primary StructureDefinitions were present and compared directly. Confidence is medium for semantic intent and terminology impact because official narrative diffs, terminology-server expansions, and cross-version ConceptMaps were not available locally.

findings.title: Page source/name model split removes R4 definition.page.name[x]

oldState.summary: A required choice element carried the page source address as url or Reference(Binary).

semanticText.definition: The source address for the page.
semanticText.comment: The publishing tool will autogenerate source for list and inject included implementations for include.

oldState.narrativeMd: `definition.page.name[x]` was mandatory and represented the page source/location. R4 JSON used either `nameUrl` or `nameReference`.

newState.summary: R6 has a required published page name URL plus an optional source[x] choice for source URL, XHTML string, or markdown.

constraints.human: Source must be absent if 'generated' is generated

semanticText.short: Name of the page when published
semanticText.definition: The url by which the page should be known when published.
semanticText.comment: The name is a local reference relative to the IG output folder; source[x] separately indicates the URL or content to provide.

newState.narrativeMd: `definition.page.name` is now the published page URL, while `source[x]` carries source content/location. `source[x]` cannot be present for generated pages.

facts.note: Added on source[x], not on name[x].

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 page model preserves a required page name but changes its meaning and introduces `source[x]` for the source-address/content role that R4 `name[x]` partly served.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct JSON shape and generated-model break. An R4 instance containing `nameReference` has no legal R6 `nameReference` element, and even `nameUrl` needs semantic review because the R4 value was the source address while R6 `name` is the published page URL. R6 inline `sourceString`/`sourceMarkdown` cannot be represented in R4 without externalizing the content.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: IG page definitions affect generated publication output; incorrect migration can publish broken or mislinked guide pages.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is reasonable: page publication tools benefit from separating the published page URL from the source location or inline content. The break is probably justified because the less-breaking design would keep an overloaded R4 field beside the clearer R6 model and would create material validation and publisher ambiguity.
justification.inferredGoal: Separate published page identity from page source and allow inline source content.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain R4 `name[x]` as a deprecated source alias while adding a separate published-page-name element and new source choices.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep `ImplementationGuide.definition.page.name[x]` with the R4 `url` and `Reference(Binary)` meanings for a transition period, then add a distinct published-name element plus `source[x]` for URL, XHTML string, or markdown source. That would preserve most R4 instances, including `nameReference`, but R6 validators and publishers would need conflict rules when legacy `name[x]`, new source, and new output-name data disagree.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old JSON but creates competing source/name fields, requires precedence rules, and risks legacy page representations persisting indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 has required `name[x]` with url and Reference(Binary) types.
R6 has required `name` of type url with definition "The url by which the page should be known when published."
R6 adds optional `source[x]` with url, string, and markdown types.
R6 adds an error invariant forbidding source when generation is generated.

examples.examplesMd: Examples are minimal fragments illustrating the changed page fields, not complete production IGs. A real migration must decide the published page name separately from the source location.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 splits the R4 page field into separate concerns. Existing R4 code that reads or writes `nameUrl`/`nameReference` will not target the correct R6 properties, and `nameReference` has no direct R6 equivalent. The biggest migration risk is not just renaming: an R4 source address may not be the same thing as the R6 published page name.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances using `nameReference` are old-valid/new-invalid because R6 removed the choice and requires `name` as a URL. R4 instances using `nameUrl` still require review because the semantic target changed. Conversely, R6 pages with inline `sourceString` or `sourceMarkdown` cannot be represented in R4 without creating an external Binary/file and using an R4 reference or URL.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map the output page identifier to R6 `definition.page.name`; map source locations/content to `source[x]` only when the page is not `generated`. Do not blindly rename `nameUrl` to `name`: test generated, HTML, markdown, XML, URL source, Binary reference, and nested page cases. Binary references generally need conversion to a source URL or external file convention.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A compatibility period retaining `name[x]` as deprecated would have allowed old JSON and generated classes to continue parsing while tools adopted the clearer model. The tradeoff is ambiguity: page tooling would need precedence rules between legacy source/name and the new separated fields.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The supplied package did not include narrative page migration guidance. Human review is recommended for IGs whose R4 page names are not already the intended published output paths.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `definition.page.name[x]` was a required choice used for the page source (`nameUrl` or `nameReference` to Binary). R6 replaces that wire shape with required `name` for the published page URL and optional `source[x]` for source content/location, with no Binary reference choice and an error rule forbidding source on generated pages. This is more than a rename: old page JSON is invalid, generated models change, and migration may require deciding whether an R4 URL was a source path or the desired published output name. Because page declarations are central to using an ImplementationGuide as an authoring/publishing artifact, the low R4 FMM does not fully neutralize the concern.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `ImplementationGuide.definition.page.name[x]` min=1, types url and Reference(Binary), definition `The source address for the page.`
R6 StructureDefinition: `ImplementationGuide.definition.page.name` min=1 type url, definition `The url by which the page should be known when published.`
R6 StructureDefinition: `ImplementationGuide.definition.page.source[x]` optional url/string/markdown; page invariant `generation='generated' implies source.empty()`
R6 local `ImplementationGuide-example.json` uses page `name` with no source, showing the new published-name shape
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 1/trial-use softens the stability expectation, but this path is central to IG page publication and migration can be lossy or expert-dependent, so it still merits renewed design attention.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen: R4 `nameUrl`/`nameReference` properties are not the R6 `name`/`source[x]` model, and page-publisher code must change behavior rather than only rename fields.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking R6 base design plausibly could have kept the R4 source choice for one transition cycle, or added a distinct published-name element while preserving old source wire names including Reference(Binary). That would preserve more R4 instances but would require conflict and precedence rules between legacy source fields and the clearer R6 name/source split.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly treats this as high-impact and identifies a partial less-breaking alternative, but the independent review puts more emphasis on the fact that even R4 `nameUrl` is a wire-shape break, not only a semantic review issue.

findings.title: Definition resource example[x] split into isExample and profile

oldState.summary: Optional choice encoded either example-ness as boolean or a single profile canonical.

semanticText.definition: If true or a reference, indicates the resource is an example instance. If a reference is present, indicates that the example is an example of the specified profile.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used `exampleBoolean` or `exampleCanonical` on each definition resource.

newState.summary: R6 separates example-ness from profile conformance and allows multiple profiles.

semanticText.definition: `isExample` says the resource is an example; `profile` lists profile(s) the instance is valid against.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses `isExample` 0..1 boolean and `profile` 0..* canonical. `profile` can be used for example and non-example resources.

facts.oldValue: one choice combined example flag and example-of profile

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 definitions preserve the two concepts formerly encoded by `example[x]`, but as independent elements with different cardinalities.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 JSON properties `exampleBoolean` and `exampleCanonical` are not valid R6 properties. R4→R6 migration is usually straightforward, but R6 can carry multiple profiles and can use profiles independently of `isExample`, which R4 cannot encode losslessly.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating example status from profile conformance and allowing multiple profiles is a reasonable R6 goal. A compatibility alias was possible, but the old choice element combined two concepts and would continue to create ambiguity when used beside the clearer `isExample` and `profile` fields.
justification.inferredGoal: Clarify example status and allow profile conformance metadata independent of example status.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `definition.resource.example[x]` while adding `isExample` and repeatable `profile`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 base design could have accepted the old `exampleBoolean` and `exampleCanonical` JSON names for one release while also adding `isExample` and `profile`. This would preserve R4 data but would require deterministic reconciliation, for example whether `exampleCanonical` implies `isExample=true` and what happens when both old and new profile fields are present with different values.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The alias preserves old instances but duplicates example/profile facts, needs conflict rules, and may leave two same-resource representations indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 defines optional `example[x]` with boolean and canonical types.
R6 adds optional `isExample` boolean.
R6 adds repeatable `profile` canonical.

examples.examplesMd: For R4 `exampleBoolean=true`, set `isExample=true`. For R4 `exampleCanonical`, migrate the canonical into `profile` and generally set `isExample=true` unless local policy says the profile annotation was not intended as example classification.

findings.narrativeMd: `definition.resource.example[x]` was removed and replaced by two fields. This affects IG source definitions, not just generated manifests. Old publishers and serializers expecting the choice element will fail against R6, while R6 publishers can now express multiple profiles for a resource.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance containing `exampleBoolean` or `exampleCanonical` is invalid against R6 because the element names no longer exist. R6 instances with multiple `profile` values or with profile metadata on a non-example resource are not cleanly representable in R4 because R4 had only a single `exampleCanonical` choice tied to example semantics.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Transform `exampleBoolean=true` to `isExample=true`; transform `exampleCanonical` to `profile[0]` and decide whether `isExample=true` is appropriate. Test resources with omitted example metadata, `false`, `true`, canonical profile, and multiple profile annotations after migration.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The split improves semantic clarity and cardinality, but a deprecated `example[x]` alias could have preserved old instances for one cycle. The alias would need conflict rules when both old and new fields appear.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 used `definition.resource.example[x]` to combine two concepts: whether the resource is an example and, optionally, the single profile it exemplifies. R6 separates those into `isExample` and repeatable `profile`. R4 instances with `exampleBoolean` or `exampleCanonical` need transformation and generated model properties change, but the R6 model is clearer and supports non-example profile assertions and multiple profiles. For this low-FMM, non-clinical metadata path, the break looks proportionate.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `ImplementationGuide.definition.resource.example[x]` optional boolean/canonical, max=1
R6 StructureDefinition: `ImplementationGuide.definition.resource.isExample` optional boolean
R6 StructureDefinition: `ImplementationGuide.definition.resource.profile` optional repeatable canonical to StructureDefinition
R6 local `ImplementationGuide-example.json` uses `definition.resource.profile`
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 1/trial-use lowers the burden for a localized authoring-metadata migration, especially because the forward transform is usually mechanical.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen: R4 `exampleBoolean`/`exampleCanonical` are removed R6 properties; R6-to-R4 loss can occur for multiple profiles or profile metadata on non-example resources.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have accepted deprecated `example[x]` aliases while adding `isExample` and `profile`, but that would duplicate the same facts and require rules for conflicts such as `exampleCanonical` versus `profile[]` or whether `exampleCanonical` always implies `isExample=true`.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing medium-impact, partial-alternative assessment matches the fresh path-level judgment.

findings.title: Manifest resource example[x] split into isExample and profile

oldState.summary: Optional manifest choice combined example flag and single profile canonical.

semanticText.definition: If true or a reference, indicates the resource is an example instance. If a reference is present, indicates that the example is an example of the specified profile.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 manifests used `exampleBoolean` or `exampleCanonical` on manifest resources.

newState.summary: R6 manifest resources use separate `isExample` and repeatable `profile` fields.

semanticText.definition: `isExample` marks an example instance; `profile` lists profile(s) the instance is valid against.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 mirrors the definition-resource split in the generated/published manifest resource entries.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The manifest change uses the same replacement pattern as `definition.resource.example[x]`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Published R4 manifests containing `exampleBoolean` or `exampleCanonical` will not validate as R6. R6 manifests can list multiple profiles for a resource, which R4 cannot represent in the former single canonical choice.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Aligning manifest resource metadata with the definition resource split is reasonable and avoids carrying the overloaded R4 choice into generated package manifests. The break was avoidable only by preserving duplicate manifest representations with nontrivial ambiguity.
justification.inferredGoal: Align generated manifest metadata with the clearer R6 resource definition metadata.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `manifest.resource.example[x]` while adding manifest `isExample` and repeatable `profile`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base option would allow R4 `manifest.resource.exampleBoolean` and `exampleCanonical` as deprecated aliases while adding `isExample` and `profile`. That would preserve old manifests, but processors would need rules for contradictions and the deprecated representation might continue to accumulate in published packages.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Compatibility aliasing would help manifest consumers parse old packages but would duplicate example/profile metadata and require conflict handling.

evidence.detail: R4 defines optional manifest `example[x]` with boolean and canonical types.
R6 adds optional manifest `isExample` boolean.
R6 adds repeatable manifest `profile` canonical.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example shows the multiple-profile case that cannot be represented in one R4 `exampleCanonical` value.

findings.narrativeMd: The same example/profile split appears in the published manifest portion of ImplementationGuide. Systems that consume manifests from packages may encounter this even if they do not process the authoring `definition` section.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `manifest.resource.exampleBoolean` and `manifest.resource.exampleCanonical` are invalid in R6. R6 multi-profile annotations are lossy when projecting to R4 because only one canonical choice was available and it implied example-of semantics.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Apply the same transform used for `definition.resource`: boolean to `isExample`; canonical to `profile` and usually `isExample=true`. Consumers should update generated manifest models and test published package manifests, not only source IG resources.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is probably justified for consistency with definition resources. A less-breaking alias was possible but would increase ambiguity in generated manifests.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The manifest-side `example[x]` change mirrors the definition-side split: R4 manifest entries used `exampleBoolean` or `exampleCanonical`, while R6 uses `isExample` and repeatable `profile`. Package manifest consumers and generated classes must update, but the migration is narrow and aligned with the clearer R6 model used for `definition.resource`.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `ImplementationGuide.manifest.resource.example[x]` optional boolean/canonical, max=1
R6 StructureDefinition: `ImplementationGuide.manifest.resource.isExample` optional boolean
R6 StructureDefinition: `ImplementationGuide.manifest.resource.profile` optional repeatable canonical
R6 local `ImplementationGuide-fhir.json` manifest resources include `isExample`; `ImplementationGuide-example.json` manifest resources include `profile`
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 1/trial-use softens the concern; this affects IG/package metadata rather than patient-facing data, and the path-level transform is generally straightforward.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen: old manifest `exampleBoolean`/`exampleCanonical` properties are invalid in R6; R6 multi-profile manifest annotations are lossy in R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A deprecated legacy alias could preserve R4 manifests for a cycle, but it would create duplicate manifest representations and conflict handling between old `example[x]` and new `isExample`/`profile`.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the current report's medium impact and partial less-breaking alternative are consistent with this review.

findings.title: Build parameter code changed from primitive code to Coding

oldState.summary: Required primitive code bound required to guide-parameter-code.

semanticText.definition: apply | path-resource | path-pages | path-tx-cache | expansion-parameter | rule-broken-links | generate-xml | generate-json | generate-turtle | html-template.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 stores the build parameter code as a JSON string such as `"apply"`.

newState.summary: Required Coding bound extensible to guide-parameter-code.

semanticText.definition: A tool-specific code that defines the parameter.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 stores the parameter code as a Coding object, allowing system/version/display and extensible tool-specific codes.

facts.note: The local CodeSystem concepts are unchanged; the break is representation and binding strength.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A primitive JSON string is invalid where R6 expects a Coding object. This is likely to affect IG publisher parameters and generated SDKs. R6 can also carry non-value-set or vendor-specific Coding values under the extensible binding, which cannot be represented as a single R4 required code without policy loss.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Build parameters influence IG publication behavior; incorrect migration can change generated artifacts.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of supporting qualified, tool-specific parameter codes is reasonable, and using the standard `Coding` datatype is the idiomatic FHIR representation. A less-breaking primitive-plus-qualifiers design would preserve old JSON but at a material long-term interoperability and consistency cost.
justification.inferredGoal: Support qualified, tool-specific implementation guide parameter codes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep primitive `parameter.code` and add optional Coding-like qualifier fields or a companion Coding.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base-compatible alternative could keep `definition.parameter.code` as a primitive code, relax its binding, and add optional system/version/display or companion Coding metadata. That would keep R4 `"code":"apply"` instances valid, but it would require processors to reconcile duplicated code values and would not be as clean as a single `Coding`.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 strings but creates a bespoke mini-Coding pattern with possible mismatches and weaker system/version/display handling.

evidence.detail: R4 type is primitive code and binding is required.
R6 type is Coding and binding is extensible.
The local guide-parameter-code CodeSystem has the same ten concept codes in R4 and R6.
evidence.quote: apply, path-resource, path-pages, path-tx-cache, expansion-parameter, rule-broken-links, generate-xml, generate-json, generate-turtle, html-template

examples.examplesMd: R4 string values should be wrapped in a Coding with the standard guide-parameter-code system when the code is one of the known HL7 codes.

findings.narrativeMd: `definition.parameter.code` is one of the clearest local representation changes: the property name is the same, but the datatype is not. Parsers that previously bound it to an enum/string must now bind it to a Coding and handle systems and non-standard codes.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `"code":"apply"` is invalid against R6 because a Coding object is required. R6 Codings using the standard system can be projected to R4 by taking `Coding.code`, but non-standard systems, versions, display text, and extensible out-of-set codes are lossy or invalid in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap known R4 code strings as `{system:"http://hl7.org/fhir/guide-parameter-code", code:"..."}`. For unknown local codes, choose an explicit tool-specific system and document whether R4 down-conversion should reject, extension-map, or collapse to a string.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible option would have kept the primitive field and added optional qualifiers. R6 instead chose the standard Coding datatype, which is cleaner but requires all serializers, validators, and publisher parameter processors to change.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `definition.parameter.code` keeps the same path name but changes representation from a primitive `code` string to a `Coding` object. That is a direct parser, serializer, and generated-SDK break for IG build parameters. Still, the R6 goal is coherent: tool-specific parameters benefit from a system-qualified Coding, and the binding is relaxed from required to extensible while the known HL7 parameter codes remain unchanged.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `ImplementationGuide.definition.parameter.code` type code, required binding to `ValueSet/guide-parameter-code|4.0.1`
R6 StructureDefinition: same path type Coding, extensible binding to `ValueSet/guide-parameter-code`
Local CodeSystem comparison: guide-parameter-code has 10 concepts in both R4 and R6 with no added or removed codes
R6 local `ImplementationGuide-example.json` encodes parameter code as `{system, code}`
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 1/trial-use softens the stability concern. The path is tooling-relevant, but not safety-critical, and the forward mapping for known codes is clear.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen: R4 JSON has `code` as a string, while R6 requires a Coding object at the same property.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could have kept primitive `code` and added optional system/version/display fields or a companion Coding, but that would create a bespoke duplicate-Coding pattern and reconciliation rules. Using the standard Coding datatype is cleaner despite the migration cost.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies a hard representation break and a partial alternative, but the fresh judgment treats the high impact as somewhat softened by low FMM and by the unchanged code list.

findings.title: Global resource type binding tracks the R6 resource set and excludes many R4 type codes

oldState.summary: Required binding to R4 resource-types value set over http://hl7.org/fhir/resource-types.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Compared local CodeSystem/ValueSet definitions, not a terminology-server expansion.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed resource type codes from the R4 resource-types CodeSystem.

newState.summary: Required binding to R6 resource-types value set with explicit R6 resource concepts from fhir-types.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: A local comparison found 41 R4 codes not present in the R6 value set and 20 R6 codes not present in the R4 resource-types CodeSystem. Some represent removed resources; others reflect consolidation or renaming.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 binds to the current R6 resource vocabulary. Codes for removed or renamed R4 resources are no longer valid, while new R6 resources become valid.

facts.note: Examples include Media, MedicationKnowledge, GraphDefinition, TestScript, RequestGroup, DocumentManifest, DeviceUseStatement, and multiple MedicinalProduct/Substance resources.
Examples include ActorDefinition, Requirements, RequestOrchestration, SubscriptionTopic, MedicinalProductDefinition, and SubstanceDefinition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The binding remains required, so an R4 IG using `global.type` for a resource code removed from the R6 resource-types value set can become invalid. The element is not always used, so this is potential rather than universal. R6 IGs using new resource codes are not R4-representable without mapping or extensions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: A bad global profile declaration can change validation assumptions for all resources of a type in an IG.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: A required binding to the current R6 resource set is reasonable because `global.type` identifies the resource type a profile applies to. Widening the base value set to include retired R4 codes would reduce validation failures but would not fully solve semantic migration when the underlying resource was removed, renamed, or consolidated.
justification.inferredGoal: Align global profile declarations with the actual R6 resource set.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Carry retired or renamed R4 resource-type codes in the R6 value set as deprecated legacy concepts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The main less-breaking base design would include R4-only resource codes as deprecated aliases or legacy concepts in the R6 resource-types value set. This would preserve old code values in some R4 IGs, but R6 processors would need special mapping rules and could otherwise accept profiles for non-R6 resource types, reducing interoperability and model consistency.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Legacy codes preserve some old globals but weaken current-release precision and can imply globals for resources that no longer exist in R6.

evidence.detail: R4 binding is required to resource-types|4.0.1.
R6 binding is required to resource-types|6.0.0-ballot4.
Local comparison found 41 R4 resource type codes absent from the R6 resource-types value set and 20 new R6 codes absent from R4.

examples.examplesMd: `Media` is illustrative of an R4 resource code not in the R6 resource-types value set. Actual migration depends on the specific resource evolution path.

findings.narrativeMd: `ImplementationGuide.global.type` is a required-code binding to the release-specific resource set. IGs that used global profiles for R4 resources that were removed, renamed, or consolidated must be reviewed because the code itself may no longer be legal in R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is a potential old-valid/new-invalid issue: only R4 IGs with affected `global.type` values fail. Strict validators will reject removed codes under the R6 required binding. R6-to-R4 conversion has the opposite problem for new R6 resource codes.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory every `global.type`; compare against the R6 resource-types value set; map renamed/consolidated resources explicitly, remove declarations for retired resources, or preserve intent with an extension/profile note when no R6 resource type exists. Test validators with each migrated global profile.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 binding is justified by model consistency. A backward-compatible value set with retired R4 concepts would make conversion easier but could mislead R6 processors into accepting globals for non-R6 resources.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: No official cross-version ConceptMap for resource-type migration was supplied; mappings such as RequestGroup to RequestOrchestration or MedicinalProduct* consolidation require domain review.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `global.type` remains a required code, but its required binding tracks the resource types available in the target FHIR release. R4 globals for resource codes removed, renamed, or consolidated by R6 can therefore fail R6 validation. That is a real potential break, but it is tightly coupled to the underlying resource model evolution; allowing obsolete resource codes in the R6 base value set would make `global.type` less precise for R6 processors.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `ImplementationGuide.global.type` required binding to `ValueSet/resource-types|4.0.1`
R6 StructureDefinition: `ImplementationGuide.global.type` required binding to `ValueSet/resource-types|6.0.0-ballot4`
Local terminology comparison: 41 R4 resource-type codes absent from the R6 value set and 20 R6 codes absent from R4
Examples of R4-only codes checked locally include Media, MedicationKnowledge, GraphDefinition, TestScript, RequestGroup, DocumentManifest, and DeviceUseStatement
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 1/trial-use softens the concern, and the element is optional at the IG level; nevertheless, affected globals can change validation assumptions for all resources of a type in an IG.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid potential: only R4 IGs using `global.type` values no longer present in the R6 resource type set fail; R6-to-R4 loss exists for new R6 resource codes.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could include retired R4 resource codes as deprecated legacy concepts, but that would allow globals for resource types that no longer exist in R6 and push complex mapping obligations onto validators and publishers. A ConceptMap is useful migration support but is not a less-breaking base design by itself.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing potential-break finding is sound, but the fresh review treats the impact as proportionate to release-specific resource evolution rather than a standalone high-concern IG design issue.

findings.title: FHIR-version binding adds R5/R6 and ballot codes that are not R4-representable

oldState.summary: Required binding to FHIR-version|4.0.1 with published versions up to R4.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 IGs can only declare FHIR versions known in the R4 FHIR-version CodeSystem.

newState.summary: Required binding to FHIR-version|6.0.0-ballot4; R4 codes remain present but many newer R5/R6 and ballot codes are added.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Local recursive CodeSystem comparison found no R4 FHIR-version codes removed from R6, but R6 adds many future and ballot version codes.

newState.narrativeMd: Forward R4→R6 validation is safe for the old FHIR-version codes checked locally, but R6 IGs that target R5/R6 cannot be represented as R4 without an extension or lossy downgrade.

facts.note: Based on local recursive CodeSystem comparison.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an R4→R6 validation break because the local R6 FHIR-version CodeSystem still includes the R4 codes. It is a high R6→R4 representability issue because a normal R6 ImplementationGuide declares an R6 fhirVersion that R4 validators do not know.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: This is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue because the local comparison found no R4 FHIR-version codes removed from the R6 binding. Allowing an R6 ImplementationGuide to identify R5/R6 and ballot target versions is necessary and reasonable.
justification.inferredGoal: Allow IGs to target current and ballot FHIR releases.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: R6 adds newer FHIR-version codes while preserving the R4 codes for R4-to-R6 validation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed to preserve R4 instances. R4 could not have native required-binding support for future FHIR release codes; using extensions or converter policy for R6-to-R4 preservation is a migration mitigation, not a backwards-compatible R6 base-design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The remaining issue is R6-to-R4 down-conversion; R4 cannot natively represent future version codes without rejection, lossy mapping, or an extension policy.

evidence.detail: R4 root fhirVersion binding is required to FHIR-version|4.0.1.
R6 root fhirVersion binding is required to FHIR-version|6.0.0-ballot4.
Local comparison found all R4 codes retained recursively in R6 and additional R5/R6/ballot codes added.

examples.examplesMd: The example is typical for an R6 ballot IG: the target FHIR version is not a valid R4 FHIR-version code.

findings.narrativeMd: The FHIR-version binding change is mostly a one-way compatibility issue. Existing R4 target-version codes remain accepted by R6 based on local CodeSystem comparison, but R6 introduces codes that an R4 model could not have known.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid `fhirVersion` code was found to become invalid in R6. Valid R6 values such as `6.0.0-ballot4` are invalid in R4 under a required binding, affecting both the root `fhirVersion` and per-resource `definition.resource.fhirVersion`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4→R6, preserve existing fhirVersion values. For R6→R4, decide whether to reject newer target versions, map to a nearest R4-supported value only with explicit semantics, or carry the true value in an extension while accepting that strict R4 validation will not see it as native.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: There is no realistic backward-compatible way for R4 to natively support future R6 codes. Cross-version extensions or converter policy are the appropriate compatibility mechanism.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding is intentionally labeled R6-to-R4; it should not be counted as an R4→R6 hard break.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The FHIR-version binding changes because R6 knows later FHIR versions. The local CodeSystem comparison found no R4 FHIR-version codes removed, so this is not an R4-to-R6 instance break. R6 instances that declare R5/R6/ballot target versions are naturally not representable as strict R4, but that reverse-direction issue is expected and does not call for R6 base-design changes.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: root and per-resource `fhirVersion` required bindings use `ValueSet/FHIR-version|4.0.1`
R6 StructureDefinition: corresponding bindings use `ValueSet/FHIR-version|6.0.0-ballot4`
Local CodeSystem comparison: 22 R4 FHIR-version codes, 63 R6 codes, zero R4 codes removed and 41 codes added
Added checked examples include `5.0.0`, `6.0.0`, and `6.0.0-ballot4`
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 1/trial-use reinforces that a reverse-only future-version representability issue should not be escalated as an R4-to-R6 concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss only: newer R6 FHIR-version codes are not valid R4 codes; no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 pattern was found.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because R4 codes remain accepted. R4 could not natively anticipate future release codes; down-conversion requires policy or extensions outside the R6 base model.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly says this is not an R4-to-R6 hard break, but the fresh judgment downgrades the action concern from medium/high reverse risk to no problem for this review scope.

findings.title: Definition.resource minimum cardinality decreased, allowing R6 definitions without resources

oldState.summary: If definition is present, at least one resource entry is required.

newState.summary: Resource entries are optional within definition.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `definition.resource` is 0..*, so a definition can contain other content without resource entries.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A minimum cardinality decrease does not invalidate existing R4 instances in R6. It does allow valid R6 IGs with definition content but no resource entries, which cannot be represented as valid R4 base instances.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of permitting lighter-weight IG definitions is reasonable, and weakening a minimum cardinality is forward-compatible for R4 instances. The compatibility concern is only R6-to-R4 representability, so a backward-compatible alternative in the R4-to-R6 base-design sense is not applicable.
justification.inferredGoal: Permit lighter-weight IG definitions without forcing a resource list.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: decreasing `definition.resource` minimum cardinality preserves R4-valid instances and only adds R6 shapes not valid in R4.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Keeping the R4 `1..*` cardinality would reduce down-conversion edge cases but would be a stricter R6 design, not a less-breaking alternative for R4-to-R6 migration. Existing R4 instances with at least one definition resource remain valid under the R6 `0..*` cardinality.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Down-converters may need to reject or synthesize resource entries for resource-less R6 definitions, but there is no R4-to-R6 break to avoid.

evidence.detail: R4 min cardinality is 1.
R6 min cardinality is 0.

examples.examplesMd: The example has definition content but no `definition.resource`; that shape is allowed by the R6 cardinality but not by R4.

findings.narrativeMd: This is not a forward breaking change. It matters for round-trip and down-conversion: R6 can express an IG definition with no resources, while R4 required at least one resource when the definition backbone was used.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid instance becomes invalid because reducing a minimum cardinality weakens validation. A valid R6 instance with no `definition.resource` cannot validate as R4 if `definition` is otherwise present.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: R4→R6 requires no action. R6→R4 converters must either synthesize a valid resource entry, omit/reshape the definition if allowed by local policy, or reject resource-less definitions as not representable.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 relaxation could have been confined to a profile, but making it base behavior is simpler for implementers who need resource-less definitions. The compatibility cost is limited to down-conversion.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The minimum cardinality of `definition.resource` decreases from 1 to 0. That widens the R6 model and cannot invalidate an R4 instance that already satisfied the R4 minimum. It only creates a possible R6-to-R4 down-conversion edge case for resource-less R6 definitions.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `ImplementationGuide.definition.resource` min=1 max=*
R6 StructureDefinition: `ImplementationGuide.definition.resource` min=0 max=*
Element type and definition remain otherwise aligned as the resource list within an IG definition
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 1/trial-use further reduces concern, but the main point is that the change is forward-compatible for R4 instances regardless of maturity.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss only: an R6 definition with no resource entries may not validate as R4; no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 mechanism exists.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable for R4-to-R6 compatibility. Keeping the R4 minimum would reduce reverse-conversion edge cases but would not preserve any additional R4-valid instances in R6.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly treats this as no forward hard break with only low reverse-direction concern.

findings.title: Publication metadata definitions shifted semantics without changing JSON shape

affectedLocation.newPath: ImplementationGuide.date / jurisdiction / publisher / experimental / copyright / copyrightLabel

oldState.summary: R4 metadata text emphasized publication date, intended jurisdiction, publisher, test usage, and copyright/use restrictions.

semanticText.definition: R4 jurisdiction was the legal/geographic region in which the IG is intended to be used; date was when the IG was published.

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 elements are structurally similar but their definitions and comments carried different business interpretation.

newState.summary: R6 metadata text emphasizes last significant change, steward/maintainer authority, stronger experimental meaning, IP ownership, and a separate copyrightLabel.

semanticText.definition: R6 jurisdiction is the jurisdiction of the maintaining authority; intended use jurisdictions are encouraged in useContext. Date is last significantly changed.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same JSON fields for several metadata items but changes how consumers should interpret them.

facts.newValue: jurisdiction of the authority that maintains the IG
responsible for release and ongoing maintenance
no version of this resource will ever be intended for genuine usage

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON shape remains largely valid, but business rules, catalogs, package governance, and UI filters that rely on these metadata fields can change behavior. The jurisdiction binding remains extensible, so the value-set canonical move is not a hard validation break by itself.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect publication/stewardship metadata can affect governance, discoverability, and legal/compliance presentation of implementation guides.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying lifecycle, stewardship, jurisdiction, and intellectual-property metadata is reasonable, but the supplied evidence does not show that existing fields had to change meaning to achieve that goal. An additive base design could preserve old business interpretation while adding the new facts, so the level of semantic breakage is not clearly justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Clarify stewardship, lifecycle, jurisdiction, and intellectual-property metadata.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Preserve R4 meanings for existing metadata fields and add distinct optional fields or useContext guidance for stewardship, last-change date, and authority jurisdiction.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 base design would keep R4 semantics for fields such as `date` as publication date and `jurisdiction` as intended-use jurisdiction, then add optional elements for last significant change, maintaining-authority jurisdiction, stewardship role, and display copyright label, or rely on explicit `useContext` patterns without redefining the old field. This is a real base-design alternative rather than converter guidance; its tradeoff is additional metadata and cross-canonical-resource consistency work.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds more metadata surface and governance rules, but avoids silent semantic drift in existing `date`, `jurisdiction`, `publisher`, `experimental`, and copyright consumers.

evidence.detail: R4 defines jurisdiction as intended use region.
evidence.quote: A legal or geographic region in which the implementation guide is intended to be used.

evidence.detail: R6 defines jurisdiction as maintaining authority region and mentions useContext for additional jurisdictions.
evidence.quote: A legal or geographic region in which the authority that maintains the resource is operating.

evidence.detail: R4 date is publication date.
evidence.quote: when the implementation guide was published

evidence.detail: R6 date is last significant change date.
evidence.quote: when the implementation guide was last significantly changed

evidence.detail: R6 adds a separate copyright label element.

examples.examplesMd: No single JSON fragment is invalid solely because of these text changes. The risk is semantic: the same `jurisdiction` or `date` value can answer a different business question in R6 than it did in R4.

findings.narrativeMd: Several local metadata elements retain their names and datatypes but no longer mean exactly the same thing. This is a semantic/conformance risk for registries, package indexes, publication workflows, and governance dashboards that treat these fields as operational metadata.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Strict structural validation usually continues to pass. Compatibility issues arise in runtime interpretation: filters for intended jurisdiction should look at `useContext` in R6 guidance, date-based publication logic may need to distinguish publication from significant-change date, and copyright display may need `copyrightLabel`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review metadata consumers rather than only serializers. For jurisdiction, decide whether R4 intended-use values should move to `useContext` while `jurisdiction` records the maintaining authority. For date, preserve publication dates in extensions or release metadata if R6 `date` is used for significant-change tracking. Populate `copyrightLabel` when display needs holder/year text separate from the legal notice.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Separate new fields for authority jurisdiction and significant-change date would have been less semantically disruptive, but R6 chose to refine existing canonical metadata. That preserves compactness but requires implementers to audit business logic.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 package did not include the external `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/jurisdiction` ValueSet, and no narrative canonical-resource guidance page was available locally.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The cited metadata fields mostly keep their wire shapes while R6 refines canonical-resource metadata semantics: `date` is last significant change rather than simply publication, `jurisdiction` is the maintaining authority's jurisdiction with intended-use jurisdiction encouraged in `useContext`, `publisher` is explicitly release/maintenance responsibility, `experimental` is more strongly lifecycle-oriented, and `copyrightLabel` is additive. These are real metadata interpretation changes, especially for registries, but they do not create an instance validation break and are largely governance/documentation clarifications.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `jurisdiction` definition is intended use region; R6 definition is authority/maintainer operating region and includes a useContext migration note
R4 StructureDefinition: `date` definition refers to when the IG was published; R6 refers to when it was last significantly changed
R4/R6 StructureDefinitions: `publisher`, `experimental`, and `copyright` keep their primitive/markdown shapes while prose changes
R6 StructureDefinition: optional `copyrightLabel` added as a short display string
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 1/trial-use materially softens stability concern. Without evidence of safety, regulatory, billing, or production harm for these metadata interpretations, the finding should not be escalated.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation plus metadata/tooling: existing JSON generally remains structurally valid, but catalog, governance, and display logic may need to reinterpret fields.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less semantically disruptive design could have preserved the R4 meanings and added separate authority-jurisdiction or last-significant-change fields, but that would expand metadata surface and diverge from the broader canonical-resource cleanup. Because this is metadata-only under low FMM, the additive alternative is not enough to make the change a revisit item.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree: the existing report reasonably noticed the semantic drift and possible additive alternative, but its medium-impact concern overstates this path-level issue under the fresh low-FMM rubric.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id/name/type, kind, abstract flag, derivation, and baseDefinition remain `ImplementationGuide`, `resource`, non-abstract, specialization of DomainResource. Status changed from draft to active but identity did not rename, split, or merge.

No local minimum-cardinality increases or maximum-cardinality decreases were found. The only material local cardinality change identified is `definition.resource` 1..* to 0..*, which is a down-conversion risk rather than an R4→R6 hard break.
`definition.resource.reference` and `manifest.resource.reference` remain required Reference elements without a new target-profile narrowing. `global.profile` remains canonical to StructureDefinition.
No local modifier flag was added or removed. `status` remains a modifier. Inherited `modifierExtension` flag/summary details are out of scope.

Local summary-flag differences were limited to explicit false/default representation in R6 or inherited elements. No material local summary inclusion/removal was identified for the changed IG-specific content.
No local slicing changes were found on ImplementationGuide elements.
No local fixed, pattern, or default value constraints were found to be added, removed, or changed.
No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex value-limit changes were found apart from warning invariants reported as notable changes.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds optional metadata elements for identifiers, version ordering, purpose, copyright label, and dependency reason
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: These additions are optional (`0..1` or `0..*`), so they do not make R4 instances invalid in R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: `identifier`, `versionAlgorithm[x]`, `purpose`, `copyrightLabel`, and `dependsOn.reason` are not native R4 elements. R6-to-R4 conversion should preserve them with extensions or accept loss.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Definition descriptions changed from string to markdown
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: FHIR JSON representation remains a primitive string and ordinary R4 text remains valid markdown in practice.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated models and renderers should treat R6 values as markdown. Down-conversion to R4 string is structurally possible but may lose the expectation that formatting is meaningful.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds/tightens warning constraints for canonical URL and machine-friendly name
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `cnl-1` on `url` and `cnl-0` on `name` are warnings, not error constraints. They do not make instances structurally invalid.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: URLs containing `|`, `#`, or spaces and single-character or unanchored-name edge cases may now warn. Tooling that treats warnings as failures should account for this policy choice.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Guide page generation, publication status, and SPDX license concept sets did not materially change
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Although value set versions/status metadata changed, local CodeSystem concept comparisons for these bindings did not show removed codes.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Version-qualified value set URLs changed to the R6 package version, but instance code values such as `draft`, `active`, `html`, `markdown`, and SPDX identifiers remain structurally compatible.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: The ImplementationGuide StructureDefinition maturity/status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is metadata about the StructureDefinition artifact, not an instance-shape change for ImplementationGuide resources.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Consumers that filter definitions by artifact status may now classify the R6 definition differently.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `ImplementationGuide.language` shows a preferred-to-required binding change in the snapshot, but this element is inherited from Resource and should be assessed in the Resource/base report.
Snapshot changes to `ele-1`, `ext-1`, and extension element constraints appear inherited from base infrastructure artifacts and are intentionally excluded from local ImplementationGuide findings.
`ImplementationGuide.global.type` migration would benefit from an official map for removed, renamed, and consolidated resource types.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4→R6 diff artifact was available locally, so rename/split rationale was inferred from StructureDefinition element definitions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An official generated diff or committee change notes for ImplementationGuide would confirm intended migration mappings.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology comparisons used local ValueSet compose and CodeSystem concepts rather than live terminology-server expansions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run R4 and R6 expansions with the same terminology server, including external terminology.hl7.org ValueSets.

analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the R4 and R6 ImplementationGuide narrative pages and any canonical-resource metadata guidance pages.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official ConceptMap was available for resource type codes removed, renamed, or consolidated between R4 and R6.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use an official cross-version resource map or migration guide for R4-to-R6 resource type evolution.
